title: World Cinema Radar — the podcast, Friday 30 October 2026

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hello, and welcome to World Cinema Radar, the podcast. I'm {A}, and it's Friday the thirtieth of October, twenty twenty-six.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And I'm {B}. <chuckle> The night before Halloween, which is exactly when you want a quiet, sensible news day. Spoiler: it is a quiet day.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It is. So we're going to be honest about that. Fewer stories, all of them checked. Today we have three big things.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: First, the James Bond casting race, which has reached screen tests. Second, the Friday openings in Spain, with a sports biopic, a French coming-of-age comedy and a very noisy action thriller. And third, the sequel to Apocalypse Z, landing on Prime Video.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Plus a short stop at the opera calendar, because the Royal Opera has a Carmen coming, and our picks for the long weekend.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One housekeeping note. Everything we say today comes from the written edition, which you can read in the app, with the sources next to each story.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So if we sound careful, it's on purpose. <chuckle> Careful is the whole job.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let's go. Bond first, because everybody is already talking about it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, the headline: Amazon MGM is reportedly running final screen tests for the next James Bond. And I want to start with the word reportedly, because that's doing a lot of work here.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. Nothing is official. Not the names, not the dates. Everything comes from anonymous sources, mostly through The Hollywood Reporter, and Dark Horizons summarised it on the twenty-second of October.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. And what does that reporting say? It says the shortlist to replace Daniel Craig includes Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor and Callum Turner.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Plus at least one name that hasn't come out yet. <chuckle> So somebody out there is keeping a secret very well.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The tests are said to be mostly in London, over the weekend of the twenty-fourth and twenty-fifth. And they cover three things: stunts, camera presence and dialogue.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which makes sense. You need someone who can run across a roof, but also someone who can sit in a room and make a line sound dangerous. |both, yes|

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Here's the part I find funny. Two names that were strongly tipped in the days before, Jacob Elordi and Jack O'Connell, are reportedly not testing at all.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So, sorry, can I say something? That's reportedly, reportedly. Same anonymous sources. Neither Amazon nor the actors have said a word.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. And Deadline, as relayed by another outlet, says that even if the tests wrap this week, there's no timeline for a final decision.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So nobody should expect a name tomorrow morning. <sigh> I know, I know. The internet will pretend otherwise.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: What is on record is the team. Denis Villeneuve is directing. Amy Pascal and David Heyman are producing, for Amazon MGM Studios.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And that's a genuinely interesting combination for this audience. Villeneuve does big, serious, patient cinema. A Bond film from him will probably not be a quip machine.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Careful, though. We can say what he has done before, but we don't know what this film will be. We just know who's attached.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Fair. Fair. My honest take is that the casting rumour is the loudest story today and the least solid one. Enjoy it, but don't repeat it as fact.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's the rule for this show. If it's a rumour, we say it's a rumour. If it's confirmed, you'll hear it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let me put the sourcing in plain words, because it matters. The first source is The Hollywood Reporter, relayed by Dark Horizons. The second is The Nation, which passes on a line attributed to Deadline.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So we have trade press, passed along, and no first-hand confirmation. That's why the edition marks it as unverified, from a single source. <chuckle> It's the most careful label we have.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And that is how I'd read every headline you see this weekend with a name and the word frontrunner in it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. If a site says it's Callum Turner, or it's Jack Lowden, or it's Josh O'Connor, ask yourself where that site got it. Because the answer is usually the same three outlets.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Also, a small point. The reports say the shortlist includes those three. They don't say it only includes those three.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right, and that is the unnamed fourth person. I find that funny. We're all arguing about three actors, and the real answer might be a fourth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It might. Or it might not. We genuinely don't know, and the honest thing is to enjoy the guessing game without pretending to win it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now, what actually opens in Spanish cinemas this Friday. Twelve titles, in total.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Twelve! And some of them we covered on Monday, like Hope, by Na Hong-jin, plus Leviticus, Wicker and Klara y el sol. So today we're looking at the others.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The first one is Karateka, directed by Aritz Moreno. It's the biopic of Sandra Sánchez, who was born in Talavera de la Reina in nineteen eighty-one.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And she won Olympic gold in kata at Tokyo twenty twenty-one. At thirty-nine years old.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Andrea Ros plays her. Patrick Criado plays her coach and husband, Jesús del Moral. Ernesto Alterio and Pilar Castro are in the cast too, and Warner Bros. España is releasing it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Now, I'll be straight. A sports biopic is not the centre of our usual taste.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: No. But I always try to say this: we found no broad professional reviews yet, so we can't tell you if it's good. We can only tell you what it is.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good. Next, for me, the most interesting title of the day. Tiempos de ilusión. The original is Juste une illusion.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And he's starting to work out love, faith, friendship and who he is. Louis Garrel and Camille Cottin are in it. A Contracorriente is distributing it in Spain.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's a comedy-drama about human relationships. Which is very close to the profile, honestly.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. No international date was found, so I can't tell you when the rest of the world gets it. But in Spain, it's tomorrow.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then there's Aniquilación, which is the Spanish title of Onslaught, by Adam Wingard. Adria Arjona and Dan Stevens, and Diamond Films is releasing it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The setup is a sniper who has to protect her daughter, and her neighbours in a trailer park, from escaped former soldiers.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the reviews in English are split. io9 sees wasted potential. JoBlo gives it six out of ten. <chuckle> Not a disaster, not a triumph.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: But both of them single out Adria Arjona. And Dan Stevens, who, let's say, goes big.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's a tactful way of putting it. <laugh>

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And two smaller ones. Esta soledad, from Javier Giner, distributed by Filmax. A couple who've separated, trying to rebuild their lives, one with a sick father and one with money trouble.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And El mundo es ansí, by Miguel Ángel Calvo Buttini, with Ramón Barea. A student writing a thesis on the writer Pío Baroja who gradually gets absorbed into his life.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One more thing on Karateka. The film follows Sandra Sánchez, but also her husband and coach, Jesús del Moral. The edition says the story is about the two of them.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's a nice angle. Elite sport is almost never one person. There's always somebody in the corner with a towel and a plan.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: <chuckle> And a stopwatch. And, in karate, a very good eye for a cleanly done kata.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Okay, I'll allow that one. <laugh>

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: On Tiempos de ilusión, I'd just add what we know about the people. Nakache and Toledano are the directors, and the film is French, from twenty twenty-six, as the listings say.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And that's the thing with a coming-of-age comedy-drama. You can't tell from a synopsis whether it's charming or sugary. That's why our confidence on it is low.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. We try to be clear: affinity with the profile is one thing, quality is another.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the others? Aniquilación and Esta soledad are both opening tomorrow too, so you have a very different set of options. One is loud and one is quiet.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which one is which? <laugh>

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I think you know. Though, to be fair, Esta soledad is a drama, and we haven't seen it, so it could surprise everyone.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Honestly? That one sounds lovely. It's a film about getting hooked on somebody else's story. And a warning: the listings don't always agree on distributors and cast, so check your cinema's session.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay, from cinemas to the sofa. Apocalipsis Z: Un nuevo mundo comes to Prime Video this Friday, the thirtieth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Amazon says it's in more than two hundred and forty countries and territories, Spain included. It also played the Sitges Film Festival on the tenth of October, in the fifty-ninth edition.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Carles Torrens is directing again. The screenplay is by Ángel Agudo, based on the novels of Manel Loureiro.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And José María Yazpik and Berta Vázquez are back. Carlos Alcaide and Julia Martínez are among the rest of the cast.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The premise, without spoilers: after the virus outbreak, the Canary Islands are the last refuge in Europe. A special mission travels to the mainland for supplies.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And one person joins that team with, let's say, questionable intentions. |ooh|

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Here's a number I like. The first film, from twenty twenty-four, is the most-watched international original film in Prime Video's history. That's Amazon's claim.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which explains the sequel. <chuckle> It's commercial survival horror, and we've not seen it. So we're only talking about context.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And a quick note on where it premiered. Sitges was the film's first stop, on the tenth of October, in the fifty-ninth edition. So the film has already had its festival audience.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The Spanish title, by the way, is Apocalipsis Z: Un nuevo mundo, and Amazon uses that wording. Some listings shorten it, so don't be surprised if you see slightly different names.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It's also worth noticing the release strategy. Same day, worldwide, on the platform. No cinema window at all.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which, in Spain, with twelve films opening in cinemas the same Friday, is probably a smart choice. <chuckle> Less competition for the zombies.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. You need a Prime Video subscription. And if you like horror on Halloween night, it's an easy one to put on.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Easy, yes. I'd say it's more popcorn than gothic. But that's fine. Not everything has to be gothic.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now our daily visit to filmed theatre and opera. And today, I have to say it plainly: no new complete recording to recommend.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We looked, and we found nothing with enough verified detail. So instead, here's what we can verify, which is the cinema calendar.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The Royal Ballet and Opera's season for twenty twenty-six, twenty-seven includes a revival of Damiano Michieletto's Carmen in November.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Götterdämmerung and Così fan tutte, both live, in February. Tosca in May. And from the Met, the new Macbeth in October, and La Fanciulla del West later on.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: But about Carmen, the dates fight each other. The official site just says November.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A cinema called Tyneside, in the UK, lists Tuesday the tenth of November. And Gwyn Hall, also in the UK, lists Sunday the fifteenth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And we don't know the conductor, the cast, or whether it's live or delayed. And we couldn't check which Spanish cinemas will show it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's an important thing. It's not a complete recording on a platform. It's a cinema event. Different thing.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The same calendar also has the Royal Ballet's Nutcracker from the first of December.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I want to explain why we don't invent anything here. A filmed performance has a lot of details: who conducts, who sings, the year it was recorded, where you can watch it from Spain.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And if we don't have those, we don't pretend. Guessing the recording year, for example, is a classic mistake. People mix up the year of the opera with the year of the recording.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. Carmen is old, the production is a revival, and none of that tells you when a cinema recording was made.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So the honest summary is: opera is coming, but we'll tell you more when there's a date we can trust.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let me give the dates in one go. Tomorrow is Friday the thirtieth. Five films open in Spain, and Apocalipsis Z arrives on Prime Video.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Saturday the thirty-first is the closing of the seventy-first Seminci in Valladolid. It runs from the twenty-third to the thirty-first, and the winners are announced at the closing gala.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: On the fourth of November, in Japan, the Tokyo International Film Festival closes its thirty-ninth edition. It started on the twenty-sixth of October.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And since Seminci closes on Saturday, one practical thing. The winners are announced at the closing gala, so Saturday night is when the festival result exists.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We don't have the jury or the winners yet. We'll cover the awards when they exist, not before.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Same for Tokyo: the edition only says it closes on the fourth of November, so that is when to look.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the tenth of November, in the UK, is the date one cinema gives for Carmen. Remember: the official site only says November.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, our picks for the long weekend. Number one, in my case, is Tiempos de ilusión.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Affinity three and a half out of five. And low confidence. Because we've not read any reviews yet.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. It's a comedy-drama about relationships and childhood, which is the kind of film this show likes. But we're honest about what we don't know.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Number two, Karateka. Two and a half out of five, low confidence. A sports biopic is outside the core of the profile.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: But you might still enjoy it. It's about a woman who won Olympic gold at thirty-nine. That's a story.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And number three, Apocalipsis Z: Un nuevo mundo. Three out of five, low confidence. It played Sitges, and it's an easy Halloween night.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One thing about confidence. All three are low, and that is not modesty. It is because we've read synopses and a few reviews, and we haven't watched the films.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. The edition never pretends we've seen something we haven't. If you watch one of them, you'll have a better opinion than ours.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And if you do, tell us what you thought. <laugh> Well, tell your friends at least.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Also, a small reminder about timing. Karateka and Tiempos de ilusión are cinema releases, so go this weekend. Apocalipsis Z is on Prime Video, so it will wait for you.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Unlike the cinemas on a long weekend. <chuckle> Go early, and book your seat.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And remember, this isn't a critics' score. It's our editorial affinity with the profile.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, the idea of the day. The Bond rumour is the loudest story and the least solid. The quiet films are the ones you can actually go and watch.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Before we go, one more time: the Bond story is a rumour, the Carmen date is unconfirmed, and the film reviews are mixed. Everything else is checked.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And that's a decent summary of a Friday. Some noise, some solid openings, and one opera that hasn't picked its date.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which is a nice thing to say on the night before Halloween. <chuckle> Go to the cinema. See something you didn't plan to see.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The full edition, with sources and every date, is in the app. See you tomorrow on the Radar.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: See you tomorrow. And happy Halloween.
